newsitem.title: USA: Cyrix unveils chip for low-cost PCs.
newsitem.headline: Cyrix unveils chip for low-cost PCs.

text.p: Cyrix Corp unveiled a low-cost microprocessor Thursday aimed at personal computer makers who want to sell PCs for less than $1,000.
Cyrix said the first company to use its MediaGX microprocessor is Compaq Computer Corp, which also unveiled on Thursday a new line of machines priced at less than $1000.

Landing Compaq, the biggest PC maker, as a customer for MediaGX is a boost for Cyrix, analysts said. The company has been struggling for the past two years to sell its chips in the face of competition from Intel Corp.

The MediaGX chip lets Cyrix chase after PC makers who are looking for ways to enter the market for machines that cost less than $1,000 -- this year's hottest category. Cyrix is lining up vendors other than Compaq for its MediaGX, said Steve Tobak, Cyrix vice president of corporate marketing.
"This is the first time a microprocessor company other than Intel is introducing a technology that is enabling PC manufacturers to enter new markets," Tobak said.

Microprocessors from Intel, the world's biggest chipmaker, appear in about 80 percent of PCs. Cyrix and a handful of other companies make microprocessors -- the type of chips that perform a PC's fundamental calculations -- that mimic Intel chips.

Cyrix will sell the MediaGX chip to PC makers for as little as $75, a fraction of what Intel charges for comparable chips. The MediaGX packs several functions of the PC, such as video and sound, on one chip, which minimizes the cost of other PC components, Tobak said.
The company, based in Richardson, Texas, will release faster versions of MediaGX later this year, Tobak said.
